paragraphs: Argyll and Bute Council's family placement team recruits and supports foster carers for children in care across the council area, and its service is shown above with the independent agencies that cover Argyll and Bute. The council needs emergency carers who take a child overnight or for a couple of days, short-term carers for a few weeks or months, long-term carers who may look after a child for the rest of their childhood, and respite carers who give full-time carers a break.

The council says it particularly needs carers for teenagers and for sibling groups who need a home where they can stay together. Its service aims include keeping brothers and sisters together when it is safe, in line with the Promise, and giving carers trauma-informed preparation, training and supervision.

To foster with the council you need to be over 21, in reasonable health, eligible to join the PVG scheme run by Disclosure Scotland, and have suitable accommodation. You can be of any gender, sexual orientation or relationship status. The first step is a preparation group where you meet experienced carers; if you then apply, the assessment includes medical and police checks and involves everyone in your household.

Every foster carer in Scotland should receive at least the Scottish Recommended Allowance for each child. For 2026-27 that is £177.68 a week for a child aged 0 to 4, £206.71 for ages 5 to 15 and £283.35 for 16 and over, with any fee for the carer paid on top by the fostering service.
Speak to two or three of the services above, including the council's family placement team, before you decide.
